'''Dicamay Agta''' is an extinct [[Aeta language]] of the northern Philippines.<ref>{{Glottolog|dica1235|Dicamay Agta}}</ref> The Dicamay Agta lived on the Dicamay River, on the western side of the Sierra Madre near [[Jones, Isabela]]. The Dicamay Agta were killed by [[Ilocano people|Ilocano]] homesteaders sometime between 1957 and 1974 (Lobel 2013:98).<ref>{{Cite thesis |last=Lobel |first=Jason William |title=Philippine and North Bornean languages: issues in description, subgrouping, and reconstruction |date=May 2013 |publisher=University of Hawaii at Manoa |url=https://scholarspace.manoa.hawaii.edu/items/397e5e9e-857a-4546-b114-8fd583fa9130}}</ref>

Richard Roe collected a Dicamay word list of 291 words in 1957.
